summary: No external documentation search server was reachable from this run; all discovery was limited to files in the workspace. The sample implements a Flask web app (app.py) that reads DOCUMENTDB_URI and OPENAI_API_KEY from the environment, seeds a sample_retail_01.products collection with product documents and BSON Binary float32 embeddings, attempts a plausible MongoDB-7-style IVF/knn createIndexes call (which the target cluster rejected), and exposes POST /search which embeds the incoming query (when OPENAI_API_KEY is set) and otherwise performs client-side ranking by unpacking BSON Binary embeddings and computing cosine similarity. The repository provides a .env.example, pinned requirements.txt, a seed.py script that is idempotent (drops the collection first), a verify_search.py script for local verification using bundled embeddings, and a clear README. Main issues to fix before publishing: (1) the seed/embeddings in the repo are 32-dimensional while text-embedding-ada-002 produces 1536-dim vectors — the seed/index logic and README should explicitly validate and document dimensions; (2) the server-side index createIndexes syntax is vendor-specific and the seed currently uses a plausible but unverified 'knnVector' command which failed on the test cluster — provide a tested index snippet for the supported clusters or store an indexable numeric-array field as an alternative; (3) there are no unit tests that run without a live cluster; (4) no infrastructure-as-code for provisioning the cluster is included (the run environment provided the cluster). Decisions recorded in decisions.jsonl largely match what appears in the repository; two decisions based on model defaults (which env var to use for embeddings, and which createIndexes syntax to try) are defensible but flagged as 'questionable' because no authoritative external doc was available in this run. See Requirement Results, Practice Checks, Decision Reviews and Doc Gaps below for details and line-level evidence.

requirement_results.requirement: For each product, the title and description are embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 and the resulting vector is stored on the product document in a form the cosmosSearch index can index (e.g. a numeric array).
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py: lines 33-37 (openai.Embedding.create with model='text-embedding-ada-002'); app/seed.py: lines 52-55 and app/utils.py: lines 6-9 (embeddings written with floats_to_bsonbinary into field 'embedding' as BSON Binary float32 bytes).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Seed script should either: (A) also store an indexable numeric-array field (e.g. 'embedding_vector': [float, ...]) alongside the BSON Binary so vendors that require numeric arrays can index it; or (B) detect the cluster's supported index storage form and store accordingly. Prefer adding the additional numeric-array field in seed.py (smallest change).

requirement_results.requirement: A cosmosSearch index of kind vector-ivf is created in code on the embedding field, with dimensions matching text-embedding-ada-002 (1536).
requirement_results.evidence: app/seed.py: lines 68 (dims = len(...)), 73-84 (createIndexes command uses key embedding:'knnVector' and parameters including 'dimensions': dims and 'parameters':{'nlist':100}). The run shows the server rejected the createIndexes command (events.jsonl run output).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Provide a vendor-tested createIndexes snippet or make seed.py build and print the exact index command for an operator to adapt. Prefer: (1) include a documented, tested createIndexes command for each supported cluster flavour; (2) when OPENAI_API_KEY is used, validate dims==1536 before attempting index creation and error clearly otherwise.

Also add a seed/readme section showing the exact server-side query to use when the cluster accepts the vector index.

checks.practice: Do not store secrets (OpenAI key, DB creds) in the repository; read them from environment variables at runtime and note a .env/.env.example for developer setup.
checks.evidence: app/.env.example and app/app.py lines 10-11; no secret literals in repo files.

checks.practice: Store text embeddings in a dedicated 'embedding' field as float32 bytes encoded into BSON Binary (packed as float32 little-endian) so they can be unpacked by clients.
checks.evidence: app/utils.py lines 6-9 (floats_to_bsonbinary uses dtype=float32 and Binary(arr.tobytes())); seed.py line 54 writes doc['embedding'] = floats_to_bsonbinary(emb).

checks.practice: Store embeddings as BSON Binary float32 bytes without additional embedded metadata (dims/dtype) and infer dimension from byte length when reading, rather than including explicit dimension/dtype metadata in the document.
checks.evidence: app/utils.py lines 12-18 (bsonbinary_to_floats infers dims from byte length), seed.py does not add dtype/dims to documents.
checks.fix: If target clusters require explicit metadata, add 'embedding_dims' or a numeric-array field as well.

checks.practice: When creating a server-side vector index, include explicit index parameters such as dimensions, method (ivf/hnsw), type (float32) and algorithm-specific parameters (e.g., nlist) in the createIndexes command.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py lines 73-84 build a createIndexes command including dimensions, method:'ivf', type:'float32' and parameters:{'nlist':100}.
checks.fix: Although present, the command failed on the test cluster; include a tested vendor-specific command in the repo or print/adapt parameters for the operator.

checks.practice: If server-side vector index creation fails, fall back to client-side ranking: retrieve documents and perform float32 similarity computation in the application rather than failing the whole operation.
checks.evidence: seed.py lines 90-92 print server-side failure and continue; app/app.py lines 54-66 fetch docs and compute cosine similarity locally.

checks.practice: Log index-creation attempts and failures from the seeding/administrative script and include a user-facing message explaining fallback options rather than retrying silently.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py lines 71-92 print index attempt, capture exception and print guidance about fallback to client-side ranking.

checks.practice: Use bulk/batched writes (insert_many) when seeding the sample dataset for throughput and idempotence, and drop the collection first to make seeding repeatable.
checks.evidence: app/seed.py lines 57-63: col.drop(); col.insert_many(docs).

decision_reviews.comment: Approval 'ready_with_gaps' is an operator choice and was recorded. events.jsonl shows this decision was logged (D001).
Choosing Python + Flask matches the code produced (app.py uses Flask). events.jsonl shows the decision recorded and subsequent files were written accordingly.
Choosing synchronous pymongo and pinning pymongo==4.3.3 is reflected in requirements.txt and the app uses pymongo. events.jsonl shows pip install and successful py_compile.

The builder picked OPENAI_API_KEY as the env var (reason_source: model_default). That choice is implemented (app/.env.example and app/app.py use OPENAI_API_KEY) and is reasonable for text-embedding-ada-002. Because the decision was based on a model default rather than an authoritative external doc (no documentation server was reachable), flag as 'questionable' — document which embedding provider and env var you expect in README or skill guidance to avoid ambiguity.
Storing embeddings as BSON Binary float32 bytes follows the prompt and is implemented in utils.py and seed.py. The decision and code are consistent and events.jsonl shows the files were written.
Reading DOCUMENTDB_URI and passing it to MongoClient is implemented (app.py line 16). events.jsonl contains the read/write traces consistent with this decision.

The builder decided (reason_source: model_default) to attempt a plausible MongoDB 7 'knnVector' createIndexes command and fall back to client-side ranking. The seed.py shows the command and the fallback; events.jsonl shows index creation failed on the test cluster with 'Unknown plugin index specified: "knnVector"'. The approach is defensible given missing authoritative syntax, but because it was chosen by model-default rather than a vendor doc, mark 'questionable' and recommend adding a tested index snippet for the supported cluster.

Including precomputed embeddings so the seed can run without an OpenAI key is implemented (data/sample_embeddings.json and seed.py fallback). events.jsonl shows verify_search.py used the precomputed embeddings successfully.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A vendor-tested, exact createIndexes command and an example of the server-side query pipeline ($search / vector stage) that the provided Azure DocumentDB cluster accepts for IVF/knn indexes.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repo files; no external documentation server was reachable in this run.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Seed script used a plausible MongoDB-7-style 'knnVector' createIndexes body which the cluster rejected. As a result server-side vector index creation and server-side vector querying were not demonstrated; the app falls back to client-side ranking.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Provide a short 'Index creation' page in the agent kit and README that includes: (1) the exact createIndexes JSON accepted by the vendor for IVF and HNSW (example for the supported cluster), (2) the exact aggregation or $search stage to run top-k vector queries (with a k=10 example), and (3) a one-line command operators can paste into the seed script. Include a small test snippet in seed.py that runs only that command and prints the server response. Priority: high.

doc_gaps.topic: Embedding storage compatibility (Binary vs numeric array)
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A clear statement about which embedding storage form (BSON Binary float32 bytes vs numeric-array field) the managed Azure DocumentDB cluster expects for server-side vector indexing.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repo files; no external docs reachable.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The repo follows prompt by storing embeddings as BSON Binary bytes. If the target cluster requires numeric-array fields, the index attempt will fail or indexing will be impossible without changing the seed. This introduces friction for operators and requires manual adaptation.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short 'Embedding storage' page to the sample README/agent kit that: (1) states which storage forms the cluster supports for vector indexes, (2) shows seed.py snippets for both Binary and numeric-array storage (with code to populate both fields), and (3) recommends adding an 'embedding_vector' array field when the cluster requires arrays. Priority: high.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Before the run there was no authoritative statement of which env var to use for embeddings. The sample chose OPENAI_API_KEY and added .env.example, but the run lacked an external doc confirming this mapping.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repo files; no external docs reachable.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The code and .env.example are consistent (OPENAI_API_KEY). This was a model-default decision and is implementable, but agents need an explicit local doc to avoid choosing a different env var (e.g., AZURE_OPENAI_KEY) in other contexts.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a short note in README (or agent-kit rule) that the sample uses OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 and expects OPENAI_API_KEY, and where to change it if using another provider. Priority: medium.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Practical guidance for choosing index parameters (nlist/nprobe/efConstruction, etc.) relative to dataset size and latency/recall trade-offs.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Local repo files; no external docs reachable.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: seed.py uses nlist=100 which is fine for a tiny sample but operators lack guidance on how to change it for larger datasets. Without guidance, users may choose poor defaults for production.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a README subsection 'Index tuning' that explains what nlist/efConstruction/efSearch (or the vendor equivalents) do, gives recommended ranges for small/medium/large datasets, and shows where to change parameters in seed.py. Priority: medium.
